Weber's view of linguistic community is a political construct that can be used to create a national society and to justify domination, but also to resist it.
language is a tool for the social construction of the nation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Weber's view on language is not only a critique of the metaphysics of language, but a critique of the national state itself.
Weber's conception of language and nation is not only relevant for the contemporary globalized era, but also that Weber was a forerunner of the linguistic turn.

The main takeaway from our work is that
language is a social construction, not an ontological given; it is a social fact, not a natural fact.
language, ethnicity, and nationhood are not given facts but are social constructions.

Weber's view of linguistic community as constructed and not given, as well as his view of language as an instrument for domination, can be a starting point to rethink the relationship of language to politics and the nation state.
